Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.hebrew: אותו מה ת"ל - בתורת כהנים תני לה, גבי פיגול: לא ירצה המקריב אותו, לא יחשב:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.english: "It" – what does the verse teach [by saying this]? - It is taught in Torat Kohanim, regarding piggul (an offering disqualified by an intention to eat it after its permitted time): "The one who offers it will not be accepted" (Leviticus 7:18), meaning it will not be credited to him.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.hebrew: מוצא שפתיך זו מצות עשה - דמסתמא הכי אמר קרא, מוצא שפתיך קיים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.english: "That which issues from your lips" – this is a positive commandment - For, presumably, this is what the verse is saying: "That which issues from your lips," fulfill it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:2.hebrew: תשמור זו מצות לא תעשה - שלא תאחר, כדר' אבין א"ר אילעי: כל מקום שנאמר השמר פן ואל כו' (מנחות דף צט:):
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:2.english: "Guard" – this is a negative commandment - That you not delay [fulfilling your vow], as [stated by] Rabbi Avin, who said in the name of Rabbi Ilai: Anywhere that it says "beware," "lest," or "do not," etc. (Menachot 99b).

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:3.hebrew: ועשית - על כרחך מכאן אזהרה לב"ד לכוף:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:3.english: "And you shall do" - Necessarily, from here [comes] a warning to the court to compel [him].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:4.hebrew: לה' אלהיך - קרא יתירא הוא לדרשה, לרבות דבר שבחובה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:4.english: To the Lord your God - This verse is superfluous, [and is there] for a homiletical derivation: to include something that is an obligation.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:5.english: "With your mouth" – this is charity - He expounds the superfluous verse [i.e., the superfluous expression "with your mouth"].

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.hebrew: מדבן עזאי נפקא - בסוף פ"ב דזבחים (דף כט.) פליג ר' אלעזר אבן עזאי, ודריש דאותו בזבח הוא מדבר, ואינו מדבר בכהן. אבל רוצה ליישב כאן אליבא דבן עזאי, וכולה סוגיא מסיק התם כמו בשמעתין. וק"ק, שהרי התם דוחק ליישב מילתא דאחרים אליבא דבן עזאי. ובתמורה בסוף אלו קדשים (תמורה דף כא: ושם) גבי ר' יוסי היה אומר ג' דברים משום ג' זקנים, משמע דבן עזאי, דמוקי היקישא דמעשר לבכור (מה בכור אינו נאכל אלא לפנים מן החומה, אף מעשר אינו נאכל אלא לפנים מן החומה), לית ליה דאחרים. וקאמר: ולרבנן דמפקי ליה לטעמא אחרינא, בכור שאינו נפסל משנה לחברתה מנא להו? ומיהו אין לחוש, אם הש"ס הולך ומיישב בכל ענין:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.english: It is derived from Ben Azzai - At the end of the second chapter of Zevachim (29a), R. Elazar disagrees with Ben Azzai, and expounds that "oto" ("it") speaks of the sacrifice, and does not speak of the kohen. But [the Gemara] wants to resolve [the matter] here according to Ben Azzai, and the entire sugya there concludes as in our passage. And it is somewhat difficult, for there it is forced to resolve the view of Acherim according to Ben Azzai. And in Temurah, at the end of [the chapter] Eilu Kodashim (Temurah 21b, and there), regarding R. Yose who would say three things in the name of three elders, it implies that Ben Azzai, who establishes the analogy of the tithe to the firstborn (just as the firstborn is eaten only within the wall, so too the tithe is eaten only within the wall), does not hold like Acherim. And [the Gemara] says: "And according to the Rabbis, who derive it from a different reason, from where do they [derive that] a firstborn is not disqualified from one year to the next?" However, there is no need to be concerned if the Gemara goes on and resolves [the matter] in any manner.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:4:1.hebrew: אא"כ מבקשים ממנו ממון ואין לו - בסוף פרק שני דזבחים (דף כט:) פי' בקונט' ממון של גזל. אבל נרא' דמיירי בנדר, כדמוכח בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף לב: ושם), דתניא ר' נתן אומר: בעון נדרים מתה אשתו של אדם, שנאמר: אם אין לך לשלם, למה יקח משכבך מתחתיך. והא דדריש הכא "בך חטא ולא באשתך חטא", מיירי במשלם אח"כ, אלא שעבר בבל תאחר:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:4:1.english: Unless they demand money from him and he has none - At the end of the second chapter of Zevachim (29b), Rashi explained in the Kuntres that this refers to money of robbery. But it appears that [the Gemara] is speaking of a vow, as is proven in the chapter "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 32b, there), for it was taught: R. Natan says: For the sin of vows, a person's wife dies, as it is stated: "If you have nothing with which to pay, why should he take your bed from under you?" And as for that which [the Gemara] expounds here, "The sin is in you, but not in your wife," it speaks of one who pays afterward, but who transgressed "you shall not delay."

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.hebrew: זו מצות עשה - דכתיב: והיוצא מפיכם תעשו (במדבר ל״ב:כ״ד):
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.english: This is a positive commandment - As it is written: "And that which has gone out of your mouth you shall do" (Numbers 32:24).
